subject: Activation playbook coordination — CobaltPay routing opt-in & OKTA SSO constraint
messages:
From: Liz Harper <liz@cobaltpay.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Arthur Kim <arthur.kim@cobaltpay.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Activation constraints — OKTA identity + opt-in routing

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're excited to move to pilot but have two blocking items before we can sign off on our prod activation window:

1) OKTA SSO enforcement — our security team requires that any UI/console access to model logs and activation controls be behind our Okta tenant (SAML). We can provide meta and an IdP test flow.

2) Opt-in routing for a subset of users — we want initial traffic to route to a dedicated warm pool but only for users who have opted-in inside our application. That implies a routing flag + ability to pin requests to dedicated residency without changing the global route.

Can Redwood support both without a product-level rollout? If not, what would be a minimal engineering scope and ETA to get a compliant activation path?

Attaching our short SSO requirements and a sketch of the opt-in UX.

Appreciate a quick read — our legal/procurement team is asking if activation can happen before EOW next week.

Best,
Liz
Director, Platform Engineering
CobaltPay

Attachments: cobalt_sso_requirements.pdf (2 pages, SAML metadata), proposed_playbook_v1.docx (1 page)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Harper <liz@cobaltpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Apr 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Activation constraints — OKTA identity + opt-in routing

Liz — thanks for the context and attachments. Looping in Ben (sales-eng/product liaison) and Marissa (runtime/product) so we can scope the minimal path. Quick answers up front: SSO for console access is something our Private customers do via IdP integrations — we need to confirm if the hosted admin UI can be SAML-bound for this account or if you will be on Private.

On opt-in routing: we have a routing flag concept in the roadmap (feature gating for dedicated residency), but it's not generally GA. We can propose a short-lived shim: a request header (x-cobalt-optin: true) that our routing layer can match to route to your dedicated warm pool. That would require a bit of engineering (routing policy + auth/telemetry) and a canary rollout.

Ben / Marissa — can you confirm effort (engineer-weeks) for: 1) console SAML binding for hosted accounts vs Private onboarding, and 2) fast-path for header-based opt-in routing combined with per-account warm-pool pinning? Also note Liz asked for ETA of 'before EOW next week' — realistic?

Thanks — Steph
Product Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

---Quoted-by: Liz Harper---
On Mon, 30 Apr 2028 at 09:12 Liz Harper wrote:

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Activation constraints — OKTA identity + opt-in routing

Quick estimate after syncing with runtime leads:

- Console SAML for hosted UI: medium-risk. Our hosted control plane currently supports OAuth OIDC for enterprise accounts; SAML binding would be an add-on and likely 2-3 engineer-weeks (auth infra + testing + support docs). If Cobalt moves to Private (VPC), it's faster (1 week) because customer-managed IdP is standard.

- Header-based opt-in routing shim: feasible as a short project. We can implement a routing rule that honors x-cobalt-optin and pins the request to a dedicated warm pool. Estimated effort: 2 engineer-weeks for routing + 1 week for telemetry and QA (3 weeks total). Caveats: needs traffic isolation review and a small config UI change to allow ops to toggle the rule per account.

- Minimal rollout plan I recommend: 1) feature-flagged internal rollout -> 2) canary with 5% of Cobalt test traffic -> 3) opt-in pilot with your QA users -> 4) full activation.

If they're asking for EOW next week, that timeline is not realistic for hosted SAML + routing in parallel. We could fast-track the routing shim only (3 weeks) and do Private/SAML discussions in parallel.

I'll volunteer to draft a mutual action plan (MAP) and resource request.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

> On Mon, Apr 30, 2028 at 11:04 AM Stephanie Nguyen wrote:
> > Liz — thanks for the context and attachments...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Liz Harper <liz@cobaltpay.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Activation constraints — OKTA identity + opt-in routing

Thanks all — quick technical note from runtime:

- Header-based routing is straightforward but we need to lock down KV cache semantics for pinned residency. If requests can be pinned to a warm worker, we must ensure KV cache isolation or risk cross-tenant leakage. That requires one small runtime change (per-account cache namespace) — estimate 1 engineer-week.

- Routing rule + warm-pool pinning: 1 engineer-week (routing matcher + config). Telemetry/QA add 1 week. So Ben's 3-week total aligns with our estimate but we can parallelize: runtime change + routing matcher in parallel (2 engineers -> 2 weeks).

- Regarding SAML for hosted UI: we can create a scoped support path (work with security & infra) but that's not the path of least resistance. If Cobalt is willing to accept Private onboarding for the pilot, we can meet their SSO requirement much faster.

Proposed ask for Redwood leadership: commit to a 2-week fast-track for the routing + residency changes (assign 2 engineers) and designate an owner to coordinate with Cobalt for the Private vs hosted SAML decision. If we get leadership OK, Ben can produce a MAP and I'll provide the runtime PR checklist.

Liz — attaching a short runtime-risk note.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runtime_risk_note.txt (1 page)
